# CANDIDATE: VIX_CONTRACT_VOLATILITY_COMPRESSION_BREAKOUT

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When VIX is very low (<12) and price contracts into a narrow range (ATR(20) < 0.25% of price for at least three consecutive 5‑min bars), a breakout on expanding volume captures the next impulsive move. The edge exists because low volatility regimes often precede expansion phases, and volume‑confirmed breakouts filter false squeezes.

## Mechanism

Compute 20‑period ATR on 5‑min bars; if VIX < 12 and ATR/close < 0.0025 for three consecutive bars, define the contraction range as the highest high and lowest low over those bars. Enter long on a close above the range high with volume > 1.5× the average 5‑min volume of the contraction period; enter short on a close below the range low with the same volume filter. Exit: chart‑stop at the opposite range extreme; target at 2× the range width added to the breakout point (or trailing chandelier exit). Only trade in the first 30 minutes after the contraction period ends to avoid stale signals.
